The disappearing peaks are most likely found at repeats. IKAROS is a transcription factor known to bind both specific regulatory elements (promoters/enhancers) and pericentromeric heterochromatin, which consists of repetitive sequences. PFA (paraformaldehyde) crosslinks proteins to DNA and proteins to proteins over short distances, while DSG (disuccinimidyl glutarate) is a longer-range crosslinker that stabilizes protein complexes. Dual fixation (PFA+DSG) heavily crosslinks the dense protein complexes at heterochromatin repeats, which can mask the antibody epitope or render the chromatin resistant to sonication, leading to loss of ChIP signal at these regions. In contrast, IKAROS binding at active promoters and enhancers occurs in more open chromatin and is less affected by over-crosslinking. Thus, the peaks that vanish upon adding DSG are predominantly at repeats.

Answer: C
